name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deep-red district with a 28-point Republican partisan lean
Incumbent Josh Brecheen renominated with a heavy financial advantage
Democratic nominee Brandon Wade raised only about $4,300 with $86 on hand
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 98 percent
model.rationale: An R+28 seat with a renominated incumbent who has out-raised his opponent roughly 57-to-1 leaves no plausible path for an upset, and prediction markets agree at about 98 percent Republican. With no public polling or outside spending in the race, the fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Brecheen.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Brecheen paired with a sudden influx of outside money for Democrats would put the outcome in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 28 points toward the GOP. Josh Brecheen, first elected in 2022, is seeking another term after clearing his primary, and he enters the fall with a decisive financial edge: about $245,000 raised and $72,000 in the bank.

Democratic nominee Brandon Wade has raised roughly $4,300 and reported under $100 on hand, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters, and no outside groups or public polls have surfaced in the contest. An independent, Ronnie Hopkins, is also on the ballot but shows no fundraising footprint. Prediction markets put Brecheen's chances near 98 percent, and the realistic question in this race is the size of the margin rather than which party wins the seat.
